patients.summary: Thirty-year-old elementary school teacher who joins the practice at 23 weeks in her second pregnancy, already followed by OB for pelvic girdle pain and fetal CMV findings, with treated iron deficiency anemia. The pregnancy brings a previa bleed, gestational hypertension, and PPROM at 32 weeks with chorioamnionitis and preterm vaginal delivery; the following year is postpartum primary care and iron repletion.

documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRICS - PRENATAL VISIT
Date of service: 06/13/2025
GA: 13w4d

S: 30 yo G2P1001 here with about two weeks of low back pain. Describes a dull ache, worse as the day goes on, spreading into both buttocks. No fall or injury. No bleeding, no cramping or tightening. Teaches elementary school and is on her feet most of the day; also has a young child at home and is worried about keeping up with both.

Meds: PNV daily, FeSO4 325 mg daily
Allergies: NKDA
PMH: iron deficiency anemia. Hx gallstones, no surgery.
FH: mother - preeclampsia. Father - HTN.
SH: never smoker, no EtOH.

O: Vitals reviewed, normal. Back: no midline or paraspinal tenderness. Lower extremity strength, sensation and reflexes intact. No rash or warmth. FHT present by Doppler, normal rate.

A/P: Pregnancy-related pelvic girdle pain.
- Reviewed what is safe in pregnancy: pace activity, sit for part of the day when she can, heat to the low back, maternity support belt.
- Acetaminophen 500 mg, 1-2 tabs q6h prn. Avoid NSAIDs.
- Return precautions for bleeding, cramping, fever, leg weakness or numbness.
- RTC 4 weeks, anatomy scan at 20 weeks.

events.reason: Routine prenatal visit, decreased fetal movement

conditions.label: Congenital cytomegalovirus infection
conditions.note: Maternal primary CMV in pregnancy with fetal intracranial and hepatic calcifications and growth restriction

reports.text:
Single live intrauterine pregnancy, cephalic. GA by LMP 20w0d. Fetal cardiac activity present, normal rate. Amniotic fluid normal.
BRAIN: bilateral periventricular echogenic foci consistent with intracranial calcifications.
ABDOMEN: echogenic foci within the fetal liver consistent with intrahepatic calcifications.
BIOMETRY: measurements lag dates; estimated fetal weight below expected for gestational age, consistent with fetal growth restriction.
PLACENTA: posterior, low-lying. Normal thickness and echotexture; no other placental abnormality.
Cervix: closed.
reports.conclusion: Intracranial and intrahepatic calcifications with fetal growth restriction, findings suspicious for congenital infection. Low-lying placenta; recommend follow-up placental localization in the third trimester.

documents.title: OB visit note 07/28/2025 (outside obstetrics)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRICS - PRENATAL VISIT
Date of service: 07/28/2025
GA: 20w0d

S: Routine visit. Feels well overall. Says this baby moves less than her first did at this point. No fever, no rash, no one sick at home or at school that she knows of. Back pain improved with belt and pacing.

Meds: PNV, FeSO4 325 mg daily, acetaminophen prn
Allergies: NKDA

O: Vitals normal. FHT normal by Doppler.

Labs (TORCH-type serology sent with today's visit): CMV IgG POSITIVE, CMV IgM POSITIVE. Rubella IgG positive / IgM negative. Toxoplasma IgG and IgM negative.

Anatomy US today: bilateral periventricular calcifications, echogenic liver foci, growth lagging (FGR). Placenta low-lying, otherwise normal appearance.

A/P:
1. Maternal CMV infection in pregnancy with fetal findings concerning for congenital CMV. Long counseling visit with patient today; she is understandably upset. Case reviewed with maternal-fetal medicine, who will follow along with us. Growth scans to continue here.
2. Low-lying placenta - repeat localization third trimester. Pelvic rest not required at this time; call for any bleeding.
3. Pelvic girdle pain - improving.
4. Iron deficiency anemia - continue FeSO4.
RTC 3-4 weeks.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT - ESTABLISH CARE

Rachel is a 30 y/o elementary school teacher, G2P1001, currently 23w1d (LMP 3/10/25, EDD 12/15/25), here to set up primary care. OB care stays with her outside OB group; MFM is also involved. She wants a PCP for the non-pregnancy side of things and for after delivery.

Pregnancy so far, per patient (records requested):
- Low back/buttock pain since late May, OB called it pelvic girdle pain. Belt, heat and pacing have helped a lot; uses acetaminophen a few times a week at most.
- At the 20-wk visit she mentioned the baby felt less active than her first. Bloodwork showed CMV IgG and IgM both positive; anatomy scan showed calcifications in the baby's brain and liver and the baby measuring small. OB and MFM are following with growth scans. She was told the placenta is low-lying and will be rechecked later.
- She did not recall being sick. Works with young kids all day and has a young child at home.

PMH: iron deficiency anemia - on ferrous sulfate 325 daily, tolerating it. Gallstones in the past, never needed surgery, no recent RUQ pain.
PSH: none.
OB hx: first pregnancy uncomplicated, term SVD; that child is healthy and developing normally.
Meds: prenatal vitamin daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother had preeclampsia; father has hypertension.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol. Teaches elementary school.

ROS: no headaches, vision change, chest pain, dyspnea, bleeding, leakage of fluid. Mood OK given the news - "trying to take it one scan at a time." PHQ-9 3.

Exam: vitals as charted. Gravid, comfortable. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen gravid, fundus consistent with dates, non-tender. Ext: no edema, no calf tenderness. Back: no midline tenderness.

A/P:
1. Pregnancy, 23w1d, high risk for fetal CMV and FGR - managed by OB/MFM. I'll stay in the loop; asked her to sign release so we get their notes.
2. Maternal CMV with fetal findings - talked through what she's been told. Nothing for us to add; she has good support from OB/MFM. Offered to be a sounding board.
3. Pelvic girdle pain of pregnancy - improving with conservative measures.
4. Iron deficiency anemia - continue FeSO4 daily; OB is checking counts.
5. Hx cholelithiasis - asymptomatic, noted.
6. Health maintenance - flu shot and Tdap due later this fall/at 27-36 wks; will do here if OB prefers. Pap/HPV done at OB in April.

RTC after delivery, sooner prn. She has the text line.

documents.title: Records request sent
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Signed release from pt scanned. Faxed request to her OB group for prenatal records, labs and imaging since April. Will route to PCP when received.

documents.title: Outside records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed OB records received today (intake labs 4/28, visits 6/13 and 7/28 with anatomy US). Prenatal panel unremarkable, O pos, antibody screen neg. CMV IgG+/IgM+ with periventricular and hepatic calcifications and FGR on 20-wk scan - consistent with what she told me. Low-lying placenta for repeat localization. Problem list updated. No action needed from our side.

documents.title: Question after reading the records
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi - I saw in the portal that my OB notes came over. Reading the ultrasound report in writing was harder than hearing it. Is there anything I should be doing differently day to day? I'm still teaching full days. Thanks for listening last week.

documents.title: RE: Question after reading the records
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Rachel, completely understandable - those reports are written for other doctors and they read very bluntly. Nothing you did caused this and there's nothing extra you need to do day to day; keep up the prenatal vitamin and iron and keep your OB/MFM appointments. Good hand washing at school is always reasonable. If you want to talk it through in person or by phone, just text and we'll find a time.

documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of visit: 09/28/2025, arrival 09:10

CC: vaginal bleeding, 28 weeks pregnant

HPI: 30 yo G2P1001 at 28w6d by LMP, prenatal care with outside OB. Woke and noticed bright red bleeding without any pain or cramping. Since then has felt the baby moving less over about the last hour. Known low-lying placenta from her 20-week ultrasound. Pregnancy also notable for maternal CMV with fetal findings under MFM follow-up. No trauma, no intercourse, no leakage of fluid.

PMH: iron deficiency anemia, pregnancy-related pelvic girdle pain. Hx gallstones.
Meds: prenatal vitamin, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Blood type O+ per prenatal records.

Exam: VS stable (see flowsheet). Alert, anxious but comfortable. Abdomen soft, non-tender, gravid, no contractions palpable. FHT 110 bpm. Sterile speculum (OB at bedside): small amount of blood pooled in the vault, no active bleeding from the os. Cervix visually closed. No tissue at the os. No digital exam performed.

Labs: Hgb 12.2, Plt 250K, PT 12.0 s, PTT 30 s.

Bedside US (OB): placenta low-lying, inferior edge close to the internal os. Fetal cardiac activity present.

Course: OB consulted and assumed care. Moved to L&D for continuous monitoring; bleeding tapered off and stopped over the next few hours, tracing acceptable per OB, movements returned.

Impression: Placenta previa (low-lying placenta) with antepartum bleeding, 28w6d.

Disposition: Discharged from L&D 16:20 per OB. Modified bed rest and strict pelvic rest. Out of work note provided. Return immediately for any bleeding, contractions, fluid, or decreased movement. OB follow-up within 1 week; repeat placental localization.

documents.title: Went to the ER yesterday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know I was in the ER yesterday for some bleeding - it was the placenta, it stopped and they sent me home from L&D in the afternoon. I'm on modified bed rest and pelvic rest until my OB says otherwise and out of school for now. They gave me the work note. Just keeping you in the loop.

documents.title: RE: Went to the ER yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know, and I'm sorry - that must have been scary. Glad it settled. Follow your OB's instructions on rest, and go straight back to L&D for any more bleeding, cramping, fluid or less movement. Your blood count there was good (12.2), so the iron is doing its job. If school needs anything else on paper from us, just ask.

documents.title: OB visit note 10/08/2025 (outside obstetrics)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRICS - PRENATAL VISIT
Date of service: 10/08/2025
GA: 30w2d

S: Seen after her 9/28 previa bleed - no further bleeding. Back pain manageable. Reports mild headaches on and off for about a week, relieved with acetaminophen. Denies visual changes, RUQ/epigastric pain. Good fetal movement.

BP at start of pregnancy 118/74.

O: BP 152/96; repeated after rest, still elevated. No edema. DTRs 2+ symmetric, no clonus. Fundi: no retinal changes. FHT normal.
UA: protein trace.
Labs today: Hgb 12.8, Plt 210K, Cr 0.8, AST 28, ALT 26.
US today: placental edge now well away from the os; no vasa previa. EFW still lagging, consistent with known FGR.

A/P:
1. Gestational hypertension, new, without severe features. Labs reassuring. No meds at this BP. Home BP log twice daily, call for >=160/110, severe headache, vision change, RUQ pain. Preeclampsia precautions reviewed in detail - mother had preeclampsia, she knows the signs. Close OB follow-up.
2. Previa resolved - bed rest and pelvic rest lifted. May return to light activity.
3. Fetal CMV / FGR - continued surveillance with MFM.
4. IDA - Hgb 12.8 on FeSO4, continue.
cc: primary care

documents.title: Home blood pressure cuff
documents.author: patient
documents.body: OB says I have gestational hypertension now and wants me checking BP at home twice a day. Is there a cuff you recommend? Wrist or arm? Good news is the placenta moved so I'm off bed rest.

documents.title: RE: Home blood pressure cuff
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad about the placenta! Get an upper-arm cuff, not wrist - any automatic one that says clinically validated is fine. Make sure the cuff size fits your arm (most come with a medium/large). Sit 5 min, feet flat, arm supported at heart level. Bring it to your next visit here and we'll check it against ours. Call OB right away for 160/110 or higher or a bad headache.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of visit: 10/20/2025, arrival 14:35

CC: "my water broke"

HPI: 30 yo G2P1001 at 32w0d. Felt a sudden large gush of clear fluid around 13:30 while at the grocery store, still dribbling. No blood. No contractions, no belly pain. Good movement. Pregnancy course: maternal CMV with fetal findings and FGR (MFM following), previa bleed 9/28 since resolved, gestational hypertension dx 10/8 not on meds. Prior pregnancy term SVD, uncomplicated.

Meds: PNV, ferrous sulfate 325 daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: T 36.8 (98.2F), BP 120/75, HR 88, RR 16. Comfortable. Abdomen soft, non-tender, gravid. Sterile speculum: clear fluid pooling in posterior fornix. Nitrazine positive. Ferning on microscopy.
FHR: baseline 140, moderate variability, no decels. Toco: no contractions.

Labs: CBC unremarkable. CRP within normal limits.

Impression: PPROM at 32w0d.

Disposition: OB at bedside. Admitted to labor & delivery for inpatient monitoring.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary (regional hospital)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - LABOR & DELIVERY
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 10/20/2025   Delivered: 10/21/2025 06:42   Discharged: 10/23/2025

Admission diagnosis: PPROM at 32w0d
Discharge diagnoses:
- Preterm premature rupture of membranes, 32w0d
- Intra-amniotic infection (chorioamnionitis) complicating PPROM
- Hypotension following epidural analgesia
- Spontaneous vaginal delivery, liveborn preterm infant, 32w1d
- Gestational hypertension
- Iron deficiency anemia
Other pregnancy history: maternal primary CMV with fetal findings and FGR; placenta previa with bleed 9/28, resolved by 10/8 ultrasound.

Allergies: NKDA

HOSPITAL COURSE:
Admitted from the ED for expectant monitoring of PPROM. That evening, roughly six hours after the rupture, she developed lower abdominal pain with continued clear leakage. No trauma or intercourse. T 38.6, HR 110, BP 110/70, RR 20. FHR baseline 160, minimal variability, no accels/decels. Speculum again showed pooling, nitrazine and fern positive. WBC 15.0 with 80% neutrophils, CRP 25 mg/L (ref <10).
On formal OB admission assessment 45 min later: T 38.6, HR 110, BP 120/75, RR 18; FHR baseline 170, minimal variability, no decels; WBC 15.0, Hgb 12.2, Plt 210K; CRP elevated. Diagnosed with intra-amniotic infection. Started IV ampicillin 2 g q6h and gentamicin 5 mg/kg q24h, acetaminophen for fever, and oxytocin augmentation for delivery.

In active labor overnight she requested an epidural, placed without immediate complication. About two hours later she had recurrent late decelerations with BP down from 120/80 to 90/60 (HR 88, RR 16). Skin warm and well perfused; no bleeding. OB called to bedside. Left lateral positioning, 500 mL LR bolus, phenylephrine 100 mcg IV. BP recovered to 112/70 within 20 minutes and the decelerations resolved.

Spontaneous vaginal delivery 10/21/2025 06:42 at 32w1d. Infant to NICU. Newborn urine CMV PCR positive, confirming congenital CMV; NICU and pediatric infectious disease following.

Postpartum: afebrile after delivery; antibiotics stopped after one postpartum dose. BP up to 140/90 on PPD1, no treatment needed, no symptoms. PPD1 Hgb 10.9. Ambulating, voiding, pain controlled. Pumping for NICU.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
- Prenatal vitamin daily (continue)
- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily (continue)
- Ibuprofen 600 mg q6h prn pain

FOLLOW-UP:
- OB BP check in 1 week; OB postpartum visit 6 weeks
- Primary care within 1-2 weeks
- Return for fever, heavy bleeding, headache, vision change, chest pain, SOB, leg swelling

documents.title: Delivery note (regional hospital)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
DELIVERY NOTE 10/21/2025
G2P1001 -> G2P1102 at 32w1d. Labor augmented with oxytocin in setting of intra-amniotic infection on ampicillin/gentamicin. Epidural analgesia; hypotension with late decels at ~03:00 treated with position change, fluid bolus and phenylephrine with resolution.
Spontaneous vaginal delivery 06:42. Liveborn preterm infant handed to the NICU team at the warmer. Placenta delivered spontaneously, intact. Perineum intact. Blood loss within normal limits. Fundus firm after delivery. Mother stable.

documents.title: Postpartum hemoglobin (regional hospital)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL LABORATORY
CBC drawn 10/22/2025 07:05 (postpartum day 1, labor & delivery).
WBC 10.8, Hgb 10.9 g/dL, platelets as reported.
Ordering: obstetrics inpatient service.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt after discharge 10/23 (delivered 10/21, 32 wks, PPROM with intrauterine infection). Discharge summary received this morning. Pt reports she feels "sore but OK." No fever. Bleeding like a period, decreasing. Taking ibuprofen 2-3x/day, iron and PNV. Home BP this am 132/84, no headache or vision change. Pumping every 3 hrs, at the NICU most of the day. Baby stable per pt. Reviewed red flags (fever, heavy bleeding, BP >=160/110, severe headache, SOB, calf pain) - she knows them. Booked TCM visit with PCP 10/29. OB BP check also scheduled.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit - 8 days postpartum

Admitted 10/20-10/23. PPROM at 32w0d, then fever and intra-amniotic infection the same evening, IV amp/gent, augmented labor, epidural complicated by hypotension and late decels that responded to fluids/phenylephrine. SVD 10/21 at 32w1d. Baby in NICU; newborn urine CMV PCR positive, so congenital CMV confirmed - peds ID involved. Discharge summary reviewed.

Today: tired, spends most days at the NICU, pumping every 3 hours. Lochia lighter. No fever, no foul discharge, no breast redness. No headache or vision change; home BPs 128-136/80-86. Pelvic/back pain much better since delivery. Mood: "a lot of crying, but mostly about the baby being in there." Sleeping in pieces. No thoughts of self-harm. PHQ-9 7.

Meds: PNV daily, FeSO4 325 daily, ibuprofen 600 prn (using 1-2x/day). NKDA.

Exam: BP 134/86 (repeat 132/86), other vitals as charted. Tired-appearing but well. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, fundus below umbilicus, non-tender. Calves soft, non-tender, no edema. Breasts not examined (no complaints).

A/P:
1. Gestational hypertension, postpartum - BPs mildly up, as expected the first weeks after delivery; no symptoms. Keep logging twice daily, OB also tracking. Call if >=150/100 or any symptoms.
2. Intra-amniotic infection, s/p delivery and antibiotics - afebrile, resolved.
3. Iron deficiency anemia, postpartum Hgb 10.9 -> recheck today. Continue FeSO4 daily with PNV (both fine with pumping). CBC + iron studies in ~6 wks.
4. Mood - PHQ-9 7, adjustment in a very hard situation, no depression criteria met today. Talked about getting sleep blocks, accepting help. Will rescreen at next visit; text anytime.
5. Congenital CMV in infant - followed by NICU/peds ID; she knows she can bring questions here.

RTC ~3 months for BP and iron, sooner prn.

documents.title: Blood count result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Rachel - your hemoglobin is 11.1, up from 10.9 in the hospital. Heading the right direction. Keep taking the iron daily and we'll check it with iron levels in early December.

documents.title: Ibuprofen and pumping
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick one - is it ok to keep taking the ibuprofen while I'm pumping? NICU nurse said probably fine but said to ask my doctor. Only taking it once a day now, mostly at night.

documents.title: RE: Ibuprofen and pumping
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, ibuprofen is one of the preferred pain relievers while pumping/breastfeeding - very little gets into milk. Fine to keep using it as needed and stop whenever you no longer need it. Hope the baby is doing well.

documents.title: Iron refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Could you send in the iron to my pharmacy? I've been buying it over the counter but my insurance will cover it with a prescription. Also - the baby came home from the NICU on Saturday!

documents.title: Refill sent
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Ferrous sulfate 325 mg tab, 1 daily, #90 with 1 refill sent to pt's pharmacy per PCP. Pt notified via portal.

documents.title: RE: Iron refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent. And that is wonderful news - welcome home to the baby.

documents.title: OB postpartum visit 12/02/2025 (outside obstetrics)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRICS - POSTPARTUM VISIT
Date of service: 12/02/2025, 6 weeks after SVD at 32w1d (PPROM, intra-amniotic infection).

Feeling better. Baby home from NICU since late November, followed by peds ID for congenital CMV. Pumping and breastfeeding. Lochia resolved. Back/pelvic pain resolved.
Home BPs normal for 2+ weeks.

BP 122/78. Breasts normal. Abdomen soft. Perineum well healed. Uterus normal size, non-tender.
Mood screen reassuring.

A/P: Normal postpartum recovery. Gestational hypertension - normotensive off meds; annual BP screening with PCP advised given gestational HTN. Pelvic girdle pain resolved. Continue PNV and iron per PCP. Routine GYN care with us yearly.
cc: primary care

documents.title: Iron and blood count results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Rachel, hemoglobin is 11.6 - continuing to climb. Your iron stores (ferritin 12) are still low, which is common after pregnancy and delivery. Keep taking the iron once a day; taking it with a little orange juice or vitamin C helps absorption, and away from coffee/tea and dairy. We'll recheck in about 3 months. OB note from last week came over - glad the recovery has been smooth.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: Electronic refill request: prenatal multivitamin tablet, 1 PO daily, #30. Patient states taking for lactation. Please authorize if appropriate.

documents.title: Refill authorized

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u BP and iron, 14 wks postpartum.

Doing much better. Baby home since late Nov, followed by pediatrics and peds ID. Still nursing/pumping. Sleep improving. Back and pelvic pain gone since delivery.
Stopped checking BP at home after OB visit, last readings all 110s-120s/70s.
Taking FeSO4 daily and PNV. No ibuprofen in weeks.
OB 12/2 postpartum note reviewed: normal recovery, BP 122/78.

PHQ-9 4 (was 7 in Oct).

Exam: BP 116/74, repeat 114/74. Well appearing. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
1. Gestational hypertension - resolved, normal BP off meds well past 12 wks. With GHTN and dad's HTN she has a higher lifetime risk; BP check at least yearly with us.
2. Pelvic girdle pain of pregnancy - resolved.
3. CMV in pregnancy - pregnancy over, closing on her list; baby's care is with pediatrics.
4. Iron deficiency anemia - Hgb 11.6, ferritin 12 in Dec. Continue FeSO4 daily. Recheck CBC/iron mid-March.
5. Mood - improved, PHQ-9 4.

Physical in the summer.
